notes: ACCESS: Tier (a) direct HTTP fetch succeeded throughout (curl with browser UA, PrestaShop site, no bot wall encountered). robots.txt is the default PrestaShop file, no anthropic/Claude-bot disallow, blanket disallow only covers controller/search/account paths - full-site fetch of category pages permitted. Site is Spanish-native (.com/es/) but has a working English locale at /uk/ (English/GBP, linked from robots.txt sitemap list and from the hreflang/canonical on every page) - all research and node-name translation done via this /uk/ locale per task instruction, so output text required no manual Spanish translation. TREE: general_sitemap_skl_gb.xml (linked from robots.txt) gave an initial category-ID list, but it proved incomplete/stale (missing at least one live category id, e.g. Table linen's own children were not resolvable via sitemap alone). Built the real tree by fetching each candidate category page directly and reading two authoritative in-HTML signals: (1) breadcrumb nav (js-breadcrumb-item chain with data-category ids) = ground truth for a node's TRUE parent, (2) the 'c-categories-links' subcategory widget shown on a parent's own page = candidate children list. Cross-checking widget entries against the breadcrumb of each candidate child revealed the widget is frequently a cross-sell/related-categories rail, not real children (e.g. Aprons and Kitchen towels appeared in Table Linen's widget but their own breadcrumbs prove they are direct children of Textile itself, not of Table Linen; Wine Rack/Umbrella Stands/Signs&MagazineRacks appeared in the Organisers widget but are actually direct children of Storage; Bed sheets' widget-listed 'children' Top sheets/Fitted sheets ARE real per breadcrumb). Every node kept in the final tree was breadcrumb-verified against its recorded parent. QTY: primary source is the category page's own JSON-LD ItemList 'numberOfItems' field; when that value hit the PrestaShop page-size cap (=50, a suspicious round number), used the on-page pagination indicator text 'You have seen X products from Y' and took Y as the true total (affected: Wall shelves 51, Walk-in closets 54, Umbrella Stands 36, Bathroom towels 73, Bathroom storage 69). EXCLUDED and why: Sale/Promotions and 'New on X' collection nodes (Textile sales, New on textile, Storage Sales, Rugs sales) - promotional cuts, not product-type categories. Large/Small rugs (size-band facet cut of the same Rugs inventory) - excluded as a cross-cutting size filter rather than a genuine product-type subcategory, to avoid conflating with the real rug-type tree. Christmas table linen - true breadcrumb parent is Christmas > Christmas Table Decorations, a seasonal/holiday collection branch, excluded per textile.md S15. Bookends, Desk bins, Waste baskets, Kitchen trash bins, Kitchen faucets, Kitchen utensils, Trays, Bathroom hooks, Towel rails, Bathroom Accessories (broad mixed bucket), Napkin rings, Garden Trash Bins - excluded as non-storage hardware/fixtures/trash receptacles/K&D or too-generic mixed accessory buckets per storage.md boundary sections. Garden pouffes, Serving trolleys, Coat racks & stands (+ its child Hangers) - excluded as Furniture/serving-purpose items. Wardrobes, Chest of Drawers, Sideboards, TV Stands (TV cabinet), Bookshelves and Cabinets (Shelves), Display cabinets, Receivers and Consoles - excluded as core Furniture (explicit Furniture examples in storage.md S21/S27); these sit one level under the site's own 'Storage' branch (Furniture > Storage) but the rule file's own worked examples classify this exact product set as Furniture, and Furniture.xlsx for this company is already complete/validated - not duplicated here. Quilts: genuine quilt products exist and cite category id 12317 (buy-quilts-) in their breadcrumb schema, but that category URL live-404s (302 -> index.php?controller=404) on both plain and redirect-following fetch - recorded as a MANUAL REVIEW leaf with null qty/link rather than fabricated. Two node placements deliberately follow product-type logic over strict breadcrumb department: Beach Towels (true breadcrumb: Garden furniture > Beach accessories) and Kids' Rugs (true breadcrumb: Kids, not Kids' Textile) are still genuinely textile products discovered via the shared research pass, so they are grouped under the nearest sensible Textile theme (Garden textiles / Kids' Textile) rather than dropped; this is flagged per-row. No Claude-in-Chrome tier needed - tier (a) HTTP was sufficient throughout, confirmed via list_connected_browsers being disconnected anyway.
